
---

title: "Get started"

---

  

The sandbox is a local [Forgejo](https://forgejo.org/) instance on your computer. It has the practice repository, the actors of the community and the CI. Nothing reaches GitHub.

  

## Requirements

  

- Docker with `docker compose` (see [Install Docker](#install-docker) if you do not have it)

- Python 3.11 or later

- Git

  

::: {.callout-warning}

The CI of the sandbox runs Docker in a privileged container. Do not start the sandbox on a computer where this is not allowed.

:::

  

## Install Docker

  

Docker runs the sandbox in isolated containers, so you do not install Forgejo yourself. If `docker compose version` already prints a version number in your terminal, skip this section.

  

### macOS

  

1. Download [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/). Choose **Apple Silicon** for M1/M2/M3/M4 Macs and **Intel** for older Macs. To check your Mac, open the Apple menu and choose **About This Mac**.

2. Open the downloaded `.dmg` file and drag Docker to the **Applications** folder.

3. Open **Docker** from the Applications folder and accept the terms.

4. Wait until the whale icon in the menu bar stops moving. Docker is then running.

  

### Windows

  

1. Download [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/) and run the installer.

2. Keep the option **Use WSL 2 instead of Hyper-V** selected. The installer sets up WSL 2 for you.

3. Restart the computer when the installer asks.

4. Open **Docker Desktop** from the Start menu and accept the terms.

5. Wait until Docker Desktop shows **Engine running** at the bottom left.

6. Run the commands of this page in **PowerShell** or in a WSL terminal.

  

::: {.callout-note}

Docker Desktop needs Windows 10 (64-bit) or Windows 11 with virtualization turned on in the BIOS. Most computers have it on by default.

:::

  

### Linux

  

Install Docker Engine with the official script:

  

```bash

curl  -fsSL  https://get.docker.com  -o  get-docker.sh

sudo  sh  get-docker.sh

```

  

Then allow your user to run Docker without `sudo`:

  

```bash

sudo  usermod  -aG  docker  $USER

```

  

Log out and log in again for this to take effect. The script installs the `docker compose` plugin too.

  

For other ways to install Docker on Linux, see the [official Docker installation guide](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/).

  

### Check the installation

  

Open a new terminal and run:

  

```bash

docker  --version

docker  compose  version

docker  run  hello-world

```

  

The first two commands print a version number. The last command prints `Hello from Docker!`. If you see all three, Docker works.

  


## Start the sandbox

  

Clone IOSS:

  

```bash

git  clone  https://github.com/florence-bockting/IOSS.git

```

  

Go to the sandbox folder:

  

```bash

cd  IOSS/sandbox

```

  

Start Forgejo:

  

```bash

docker  compose  up  -d

```

  

Create the users, the repository and the issues:

  

```bash

python3  setup.py

```

  

The first CI job takes about 5 minutes, because Docker downloads the images. Later jobs take less than 1 minute.

  

## Log in

  

1. Open <http://localhost:3000/tinystats/tinystats>.

2. Log in as `newcomer`. The password is in the file `.env`:

  

```bash

grep NEWCOMER_PASSWORD .env

```

  

## Play

  

-  **The tour** starts on your first visit to the repository. The **Start tour** button at the bottom right starts it again.

-  **The quest issue** is pinned in the issue list. It shows your tasks as a checklist. When you finish a task, the bot ticks the box and names the next task.

-  **The actors** answer you. For example, the maintainer assigns an issue to you when you write that you want to work on it.

  

The steps of the game are in the [scenario file](https://github.com/florence-bockting/IOSS/blob/main/scenarios/first-contribution.md).

  

## Start again

  

::: {.callout-warning}

This deletes all users, issues and pull requests of the sandbox.

:::

  

```bash

docker  compose  down  -v

```

  

```bash

rm  .env

```

  

Then start the sandbox again.

The [sandbox README](https://github.com/florence-bockting/IOSS/blob/main/sandbox/README.md) explains the CI, the tour and the quest in detail.
